title: Mini Chronicle: Cost Lens for Batch & Cache Policies
creator: Lena Chen
description: Problem: engineering teams struggle to interpret how batching and prefix/KV cache settings translate into dollars and latency for mixed workloads. Goal: ship a compact, context-aware cost lens inside the Redwood Console that surfaces per-route estimated savings, guardrail risk indicators, and one-click experiment scaffolding (A/B canary) for safe rollout of suggested batch/cache presets.
background: Research sessions with three customers (search-app, chat-saas, summarization-poc) showed confusion between per-token unit cost and effective per-request latency at 95th percentile. Existing recommendation cards are high-fidelity but too wide; teams wanted a compact inline lens that fits next to route attribution and rollout controls.
acceptance_criteria: Compact cost lens component exists in the route detail header and can expand to a mini-panel
Lens shows: current cost estimate, suggested preset, projected delta (tokens and $) for 7d and 30d, and a risk score for quality/regression
Guardrail indicators present: latency impact, top-5 failure modes, confidence band, and recommended rollback thresholds
One-click 'Scaffold Experiment' button creates canary with suggested rollout rules and links to deployment view
Design reviewed by PM and Runtime Eng and its Figma prototype validated with 5 usability sessions (internal+customer), with >80% task completion for applying suggestion
Accessibility: keyboard focus order and color contrast validated
prototype_notes: Initial compact card designed to occupy a 320x136 slot next to the route summary
Collapsed state: shows current $/k tokens and 7d projected delta badge (+/-) plus a colored risk dot
Expanded state: inline sparkline for cost trend, stacked breakdown (tokens, compute, caching hit-rate), and a small table comparing current vs suggested preset
Interactive control: 'Simulate' slider (0-100% traffic) updates projected savings and latency estimates in real-time
engineering_feedback: Tomás Rivera (Runtime): prefer server-side estimate endpoint to avoid client skew; suggested percentiles for latency should use p95 from trace store
Marcus O'Neil (Backend): add memoized API for suggested presets API; avoid heavy calculations on page load
Decision from Eng: initial MVP will use approximate cost model (token-rate * model-cost + cache-hit heuristics) with nightly re-eval for accuracy
pm_feedback: Priya Singh (PM): prioritize clear rollback copy and explicit canary scaffolding; customers worry about accidental global policy changes
PM requested metrics to tie to 'savings realized' and 'quality regressions' for post-rollout audits
usability_findings: Participants misinterpreted 'confidence band' when shown without inline explanation; added microcopy and an info tooltip
Users wanted both absolute $ and percentage savings—updated panels to show both
Non-technical product manager asked for a one-line 'Impact Summary' for exec comms; added a compact sentence to expanded view
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Show estimates (vs hard guarantees): we display 'Projected' prefix and a confidence icon to avoid SLA misunderstandings
Auto-apply presets vs suggestion-only: chosen path is suggestion-only for MVP; an 'Apply Automatically' opt-in will be scoped to Dedicated customers in a later release
Data freshness vs cost: use cached estimates to keep console responsive; provide a 'Recompute now' action
reviews: 2025-11-10 - Design review with Eng & PM: accepted with notes on API surface and microcopy
2025-11-14 - Accessibility pass by UX: contrast issues fixed; keyboard order validated
2025-11-18 - Prototype usability run (5 participants): minor microcopy changes and tooltip added
risks: Estimates may diverge for bursty workloads leading to mistrust; mitigation: show recent error bars and a link to raw metric query
Overloading the route header with too much data; mitigation: collapsed default and progressive disclosure
Customers could misapply presets across routes; mitigation: scaffolded canary creation and explicit confirmation flow
next_steps: Finalize Figma screens for development handoff by 2025-11-24
Backend: runtime team to expose /estimate-cost endpoint (ENG-5219) - blocker until schema agreed
Implement MVP front-end with feature flag and write Cypress smoke tests
Schedule customer alpha with 2 pilot accounts in Dec 2025
notes_for_dev_hand_off: Provide JSON schema for the estimate endpoint: {route_id, suggested_preset, projected_delta_7d, projected_delta_30d, confidence}
Include example payload in Confluence doc and mock server for local dev
Frame microcopy keys in i18n strings to support translation
